description:
FILED s477 (Fable, 2026-09-07) from the s473d review probes.  PRE-EXISTING: identical on main 37b7e83b and on the s473d tree (0c90e681); s473d's #1230/#1245 change (the :DUAL marker) did not move it, because the errno-0 read never builds the dualvar box in the first place.

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  use Scalar::Util qw(isdual);
  $! = 2; print isdual($!) ? "dual" : "plain";   # dual on both
  $! = 0; print isdual($!) ? "dual" : "plain";   # perl: dual   PCL: plain
  my $c = $!; print isdual($c) ? "dual" : "plain";   # perl: dual   PCL: plain

Cause (read, not yet probed at the line): p-errno-string builds the :dual box under a condition that skips errno 0 (the hunk at cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~1615 sits inside a branch), so the errno-0 read hands back a plain "" / 0.  Perl's $! magic sets both IV and PV on every get, so isdual is true for every errno including 0.

Fix shape: build the dualvar box for errno 0 too (nv 0, sv ""), i.e. make the :dual marker unconditional at that ONE writer; guard row beside numeric-repr-01.t's dualvar rows (isdual($!) at errno 0 and its copy), inverse-verified.  Low priority: only Scalar::Util::isdual observes it; `$!+0`, `"$!"` and boolean tests of an errno-0 `$!` already agree with perl.
subject: Scalar::Util::isdual($!) is FALSE in PCL when errno is 0 (perl: true -- $! is ALWAYS a dualvar, "" / 0), and a copy `my $c = $!` of the errno-0 value is plain too; with errno 2 both agree
